902.s: He cites Candido at 98, Lionel Hampton and Clark Terry as proof that music heals and keeps people young.
902.q: Oh yeah. You know we just had this conversation and, back at the room over there at the hotel this morning. Because we were talking about Lionel Hampton and how these guys, when they get to their instrument, you had to help him up on stage but when he gets to the instruments he feels no pain and…

1029.t: Setting goals and keeping a schedule
1029.s: A recording project is delayed, but personal goals like exercise continue; he keeps a schedule with an exercise bike.
1029.q: Wow I just feel like there’s some goals that I have not moved. In other words I’ve got goals I want to attain so it puts a little more pressure on me just to find a way to attain the goal during this situation. Some, like this recording project I’m going to be getting started on but because we’re…

503.s: Looking at Wilson at 91, he says you are as old as you feel.
503.q: …and he just is as spry as anybody I know and loves jazz. He was a(n) alto player for a while but gave it up for other things. But the point is I guess you’re as old as you feel…

408.t: Facing death and enjoying each day
408.q: [chuckles] It’s the last thing I’m going to do. [MN laughs] But I, I don’t, you know death is a part, I mean, it’s something we all have to face and with our eyes wide open and straight ahead. Yeah, you can die, man. So get your shit together, man. And from that point of view, I don’t have any fear…

67.s: He will play until he cannot play another note, even with false teeth from his dentist brother.
67.q: Well, I guess the day that I can't play another note. That'll be the day. Because I still like playing and I'm going to play as long as I can -- as long as I have the wind. And the teeth, and if the teeth go before the wind, then I'll go downtown, down to Nashville, my brother's

70.t: Pops Smith's long career and late-life Tenderly
70.s: Pops, the best of the brothers, played first trumpet with Fletcher for years, retired with Calloway at 66 and played beautifully into his eighties.
70.ch: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
70.q: Pops to me was the greatest of the three. He played first trumpet with Fletcher for years and years and years and years. He played -- he come in the band before Don left the band to go to McKinney. So Don left the band in '27. So Pops had to be there in '27, you know.

234.t: Aging artists: Rudolph, Lee Whipper and Eubie Blake
234.s: Johnston and Gil talk about very old performers who are still active.

386.t: Age, health and helping older people
386.s: At 71 he wonders how long he will live and says he helps older people across the street.
386.q: To play for 53 years and to continue to play make'me wonder how old I'm going to get. I don't know...I'm 71 now. I'm in my 72nd year. Maybe I'm going to follow Eubie Blake. I don't need my glasses to read...I don't use my glasses to read.

95.s: She jokes about boyfriends and her children, mentions arthritis and a cane, and says being active keeps her feeling sixteen at eighty.
95.q: (Unintelligible) somebody promised to be. I got a whole lot of people promised to be. But I got children, I can't have no boyfriends because of my children. They're watching you every -- I ________ me in the bed with a man there. They come there (unintelligible). I say, they think they smart, but…

97.t: Band leaders handing over; age and Eubie Blake
97.s: Age limits playing, unlike Eubie Blake.
97.q: There you are. Just like this guy Lawrence Welk. He has an assistant leader. He starts them off and then gets over to the side. He announces what's coming on and all like that. And he lets this other guy take over.

413.s: Eubie, age 96, can't find a piano.
413.q: I feel a little better now. 96 years old and he still has to practice. I don't feel so bad about having to still practice, because I'm only 62.

239.t: Butter, Fletcher Henderson, and Eubie Blake's undimmed hands
239.s: Butter's early career, then musicians who keep their ability, with Eubie Blake as the example.
239.ch: Stuff Smith Trio and New York
239.q: You know, barring bad health or something like that, you know. As we've noticed with Eubie Blake. That's a crowning example.
